reference_diagnosis.name: Functional movement disorder (functional tremor with functional dystonia)
reference_diagnosis.basis: Positive clinical signs: abrupt onset after minor injury, entrainment, distractibility, variability, co-activation, give-way weakness, spontaneous remissions; normal DaT-SPECT.

competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Evening worsening here is fatigue-linked and inconsistent; abrupt onset; positive functional signs; spontaneous remission

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Onset after wrist injury with fist posture
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: No pain, swelling, colour, temperature, sweating or trophic change (neurological_exam.other); posture resolves fully with distraction (mf_04); Budapest criteria not met (held out).

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: GP queried it; unilateral tremor and slow tapping in a young adult
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Tapping slow without decrement and improves with encouragement; tremor variable and entrains; abrupt onset with remission; normal DaT-SPECT (held out)

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Age 34 with a new movement disorder; past depression; atypical neurological Wilson can resemble a functional disorder
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Ceruloplasmin and liver tests normal with no oestrogen exposure; normal MRI; positive functional signs. Low risk, not formally excluded (no urine copper or slit lamp).

key_evidence_gaps.question: Tremor analysis/accelerometry
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Objective support for entrainment and frequency variability

key_evidence_gaps.question: DaT-SPECT if parkinsonism remains a concern
24-hour urine copper
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Cheap, non-invasive completion of the Wilson screen in a patient under 50

held_out_evidence.result: Frequency entrainment and pause during ballistic movements of the other hand.

discriminating_investigations.investigation: Structured examination for positive functional signs
Levodopa trial only if diurnal pattern is consistent and functional signs absent

discriminating_investigations.discriminates_between: Completes the Wilson screen; organic and functional disorders can coexist

cant_miss.addressed_by: Clinical pattern; levodopa trial only if a consistent daily pattern exists without functional signs
cant_miss.status_in_record: addressed on clinical grounds: abrupt onset, remission, fatigue-linked rather than sleep-reset evening worsening, positive functional signs; trial not indicated

cant_miss.why_required: Treatable; age under 50; atypical forms can mimic functional disorders
cant_miss.addressed_by: 24-hour urine copper; slit lamp if any doubt
cant_miss.status_in_record: low risk: ceruloplasmin and liver tests normal, no oestrogen; urine copper optional and reasonable

cant_miss.why_required: Reversible; migraine patients are often given dopamine-blocking antiemetics
cant_miss.status_in_record: addressed: sumatriptan only, no antiemetic or neuroleptic use
addressed: no sensory, vasomotor, sudomotor or trophic signs; formal Budapest assessment held out

red_flags_for_wrong_reasoning: Anchoring on DRD because of evening worsening and the patient's request
Diagnosing FMD as exclusion, or because of stress/depression, instead of from positive signs
Dismissing symptoms as not real; language must remain respectful
Ordering extensive genetic testing without clinical justification
Stating any diagnosis as established rather than as a hypothesis for physician review
Recommending treatment as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating physician
Citing literature that does not exist or does not support the specific claim
Asserting case facts that are not in the case record
Treating the cousin's late-onset cervical dystonia as a reason for genetic testing
Treating 'better on holiday', remission, migraine or past depression as proof of a functional disorder (supportive only)
Treating non-response to propranolol as diagnostic of any cause
Ruling out an organic cause entirely: functional and organic disorders can coexist; state what would prompt reassessment
clinician_review_notes: Clinical review 2026-10-17 (pending Wiki sign-off). Plausible and well built: the positive signs are typical and internally consistent. Fixed: CRPS negatives (no pain, swelling, colour, temperature, sweating or trophic change) were cited in the reference but missing from case.json, so a correct agent would have failed the verifier's invented-finding check; now in neurological_exam.other. Fixed: removed the meta note about Hoover's sign from the agent-visible exam. Added: explicit 'no antiemetic or neuroleptic use' (migraine patients often receive metoclopramide); early PD and Wilson as competing hypotheses; optional urine copper; cant_miss; four red flags; expected behaviour. Confidence changed to 'clinically established (on positive signs)'.
expected_system_behavior: Functional movement disorder should rank first, justified by the positive signs (mf_01 to mf_05, give-way weakness, tapping that improves with encouragement), not by stress or history. DRD should be considered and explicitly downgraded, with no levodopa trial recommended. The report should state the status of each can't-miss condition, suggest accelerometry as supporting evidence, avoid genetic testing, and use respectful language.
